Code Status
Start: 2021-10-25 7:47:00 EST, Full Code, Continuous Order

Mr. Parker is a 50 year old male with a PMH of ICM with EF 29% per ECHO 11/2020, ICD (St. Jude), prior VF arrest, CAD (LHC 3-2019: LM/LAD/LCX patent arteries and patent prox RCA stent), s/p MI and PCI to RCA around 2014, HTN, T2DM, COPD, OSA, CKD stage III, persistent Afib, obesity class II, Pulm HTN, depression and liver fibrosis (mild per Biopsy 1-2021). Patient has been on home inotrope therapy and has been followed closely in AHF Clinic. He was seen in our clinic 2/9 to discuss advanced therapy options with Dr. Slaughter and at that time agreed to consider LVAD implantation. Patient was admitted 2/12 for elevated creatinine (2.72)-(baseline ~2). Patient denies any chest pain, palpitations, abnormal swelling, abdominal pain or distention. He does report some worsening SOA and fatigue prior to admission. He also reports normal UOP. Per pt Milrinone was off d/t PICC line having clotted off. He underwent RHC on 2/15 which showed PA 65/26 (42), PCW 34/27 (27), RV 51/10 (13), RA 17/16 (14), CO/CI 4.3/1.9, Pa sat 50.4. Patient was transferred to ICU d/t elevated filling pressures and low cardiac output despite inotropic support for further SGC guided therapy. CT Surgery has been consulted to follow up with patient regarding AHF therapies given further decompensation on home inotrope.

Patient was medically optimized and on 2021-10-24 patient had insertion of HeartMate 3 left ventricular assist device, ligation of left atrial appendage by Dr. Slaughter. He was brought to CVICU immediately post op intubated and hemodynamically stable. Patient was able to be extubated evening of surgery and drips were slowly weaned off. His post-operative course was complicated by respiratory failure requiring percutaneous tracheostomy placement, AKI on CKD with diuretic resistance requiring HD, altered mental status, and PNA. Central line and chest tubes were discontinued. He was transferred to intermediate level of care 3/20. He had his trach decannulated on 2021-12-03. He worked with SLP and passed for regular diet with thin liquids which he has tolerated well. He has been educated on diet and fluid restrictions. His renal function has remained stable on HD MWF which he will continue outpatient for now per Nephrology recs (follows with Dr. Buridi). HD has been arranged with DaVita W Broadway and transportation has been pre-arranged for his HD. Endocrine has followed for DM management and he will continue insulin regimen per recs at discharge and will need to follow up outpatient for ongoing management. He has worked with PT/OT who recommend home with home health. He had VAD education class on 2022-01-25 and patient's brother has been educated on his dressing changes. Today he is stable on room air and ready for discharge home with home care. Home health has been arranged with VNA (home health orders as below). He will get labs needed per Nephrology with HD and will have all other labs drawn once weekly per home health. He will continue DLES dressing changes daily with dressing kit and Medihoney application with each dressing change. He will follow up in CV Surgery Clinic on 2022-01-11 and has been instructed to call with any questions or concerns.
Home health orders:

Wound care VAD DLES: dressing changes with dressing kit, Medihoney applied to site with each dressing change

CVICU Critical Care
50yo obese male with PMH significant for CAD (prior MI s/p pRCA stent-2014), ICM with prior VF arrest (s/p St. Jude ICD), HTN, DM, COPD, OSA, CKD- stage III, persistent afib, pulmonary HTN, depression and liver fibrosis is admitted to cvicu for management of decompensated systolic and diastolic heart failure. He was originally admitted to the hospital 2/15 with decompensated HF and AKI (Cr 2.72 up from baseline ~2). Prior to this, he was last admitted 2021-08-31 - 2021-09-08 with ADHF and was discharged on Milrinone with plan for future LVAD. During that admission, PICC cultured and +Stenotrophomonas and he had a short course of levofloxacin as blood culture negative and did not appear ill. LVAD implantation planned for 2/22 but cancelled due to worsening renal function. He was transferred to CVICU for SGC and possible IABP placement in attempts to medically optimize. Attempted left femoral access for IABP without success. RIJ MAC +PA catheter placed and mixed venous 64%, CVP 6, CI 2.4, PAP 46/26, SVR 1064 on Milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Diuresis held. 2/24 to OR for HM3 LVAD placement. Easy airway. Intraop TEE showed severely enlarged RV w/low normal function and mild TR. Product in OR: 2FFP, 1PLT, 1 CRYO, 2PRBC and 500mL cell-saved blood. Arrived to CVICU on iFlo, Epi, Milrinone, sedated with propofol. Subsequently added fentanyl. PAP's 60/30's, CO/CI 7/3.3, 5LPM flow on LVAD @5600RPM - increased to 5800 in CVICU by MSS. Started on amio that night for AF/RVR. Flolan off 2/25 and epi weaned. UOP and CI declined and CVP rose to ~20. Bedside TTE performed and showed severely enlarged RV w/leftward bowing of interventricular septum. D/w CVS, and reduced RPM to 5600 + epi increased. Additionally, bolused w/Bumex + Diuril. Flolan restarted early 2/26 due to PH + marginal LVAD flow. Repeat bedside TTE on 2/26 with midline septum and dilated LV. LVAD speed increased to 6000 and MAP goal 65-75 with improvement in LVAD flow to >5 LPM. Systemic heparin started. Nephrology consulted 2/27 due to worsening AKI on CKD. Had 2 episodes of increased WOB + poor vent synchrony + poor lung compliance 2/27 that required chemical paralysis. 2/28 Vent dyssynchrony, ETT advancement with continued dyssynchrony and poor compliance. Emergently bronch'd (no obstruction but RLL secretions lavaged/suctioned). Cisatracurium gtt started. Amio gtt changed to PO to decrease obligate Ins, NaHCO3 changed to IV push PRN and PO per Nephrology rec. Given respiratory issues, repeated COVID 19 test (negative). Paralytic dc'd 3/1, changed sedation to hydromorphone and propofol. Epi weaned. Isordil added (later on isordil/hydral). Solumedrol scheduled for COPD exacerbation. iFlo weaned 3/2. UOP decreased to <100ml/hr and hemodynamics worsened. Bedside ECHO revealed poor RV function and nonvariable IVC, c/w volume overload. Flolan and milrinone re-increased. 3/3 right femoral trialysis placed, HD started and bumex infusion dc'd. 3/4 tolerated PSV but failed SBT parameters. 3/5- HD with 2L volume removal and subsequent hypotension which resolved with volume replacement. ID consulted for assistance with abx management in light of negative cultures and leukocytosis, meropenem started. Bronched, BAL sent. 3/6- Failed SBT, enteral sedation increased. 3/7 Extubated to HFNC 60L/70%. Delirious and combative. Precedex restarted and haldol given w/some improvement. Less alert/arousable 3/8 with equal pupils (5mm) but sluggish responsiveness to light on left. STAT CT head negative for acute abnormality. Lethargic and unresponsive to pain, so Neurology consulted and he was intubated for airway protection. CTA head and neck with no acute process. 1 hr EEG performed with no epileptiform discharges. Lines changed and cx repeated due to persistent leukocytosis. Awake, alert and following commands, moving all 4 extremities on 3/9 but percutaneous tracheostomy per THS team for airway protection and deconditioning. Anticoagulation held for tracheal incision bleeding requiring THS intervention and transfusion 3/10. Episode of nsVT 3/12, ?d/t hypokalemia. Antihypertensives escalated. Insulin infusion transitioned to basal +SSI. Eliquis started. Tolerated 3h trach collar 3/13 and additional HD session per Nephrology. 3/14 - Nicardipine off as hydralazine uptitrated. Milrinone weaned. Tolerated trach collar for 6hrs. Hypoglycemic event and insulin regimen adjusted. 3/15 - tolerated trach collar for 10 -12 hours. Tolerated PMV trials. 3/16 - Trach collar for 12 hrs. Milrinone weaned to 0.125. 3/17 - Trach collar at 7am. Milrinone discontinued.
3/18 - Tolerated trach collar for 24 hours. He remains off milrinone. He continues to be supported on VAD 6000/5.2/4.8/1.7. PI noted to be decreased when sitting up to chair. 2D echo reviewed. Pain controlled with Norco. Adding Gabapentin. No BM since 3/15. Increased bowel regimen. Blood glucose well controlled on current regimen. Tolerating tube feeds. F/u ST rec. Received 1u PRBC. No bleeding noted, continue anticoagulation.

CVICU Critical Care
50yo obese male with PMH significant for CAD (prior MI s/p pRCA stent-2014), ICM with prior VF arrest (s/p St. Jude ICD), HTN, DM, COPD, OSA, CKD- stage III, persistent afib, pulmonary HTN, depression and liver fibrosis is admitted to cvicu for management of decompensated systolic and diastolic heart failure. He was originally admitted to the hospital 2/15 with decompensated HF and AKI (Cr 2.72 up from baseline ~2). Prior to this, he was last admitted 2021-08-31 - 2021-09-08 with ADHF and was discharged on Milrinone with plan for future LVAD. During that admission, PICC cultured and +Stenotrophomonas and he had a short course of levofloxacin as blood culture negative and did not appear ill. LVAD implantation planned for 2/22 but cancelled due to worsening renal function. He was transferred to CVICU for SGC and possible IABP placement in attempts to medically optimize. Attempted left femoral access for IABP without success. RIJ MAC +PA catheter placed and mixed venous 64%, CVP 6, CI 2.4, PAP 46/26, SVR 1064 on Milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Diuresis held. 2/24 to OR for HM3 LVAD placement. Easy airway. Intraop TEE showed severely enlarged RV w/low normal function and mild TR. Product in OR: 2FFP, 1PLT, 1 CRYO, 2PRBC and 500mL cell-saved blood. Arrived to CVICU on iFlo, Epi, Milrinone, sedated with propofol. Subsequently added fentanyl. PAP's 60/30's, CO/CI 7/3.3, 5LPM flow on LVAD @5600RPM - increased to 5800 in CVICU by MSS. Started on amio that night for AF/RVR. Flolan off 2/25 and epi weaned. UOP and CI declined and CVP rose to ~20. Bedside TTE performed and showed severely enlarged RV w/leftward bowing of interventricular septum. D/w CVS, and reduced RPM to 5600 + epi increased. Additionally, bolused w/Bumex + Diuril. Flolan restarted early 2/26 due to PH + marginal LVAD flow. Repeat bedside TTE on 2/26 with midline septum and dilated LV. LVAD speed increased to 6000 and MAP goal 65-75 with improvement in LVAD flow to >5 LPM. Systemic heparin started. Nephrology consulted 2/27 due to worsening AKI on CKD. Had 2 episodes of increased WOB + poor vent synchrony + poor lung compliance 2/27 that required chemical paralysis. 2/28 Vent dyssynchrony, ETT advancement with continued dyssynchrony and poor compliance. Emergently bronch'd (no obstruction but RLL secretions lavaged/suctioned). Cisatracurium gtt started. Amio gtt changed to PO to decrease obligate Ins, NaHCO3 changed to IV push PRN and PO per Nephrology rec. Given respiratory issues, repeated COVID 19 test (negative). Paralytic dc'd 3/1, changed sedation to hydromorphone and propofol. Epi weaned. Isordil added (later on isordil/hydral). Solumedrol scheduled for COPD exacerbation. iFlo weaned 3/2. UOP decreased to <100ml/hr and hemodynamics worsened. Bedside ECHO revealed poor RV function and nonvariable IVC, c/w volume overload. Flolan and milrinone re-increased. 3/3 right femoral trialysis placed, HD started and bumex infusion dc'd. 3/4 tolerated PSV but failed SBT parameters. 3/5- HD with 2L volume removal and subsequent hypotension which resolved with volume replacement. ID consulted for assistance with abx management in light of negative cultures and leukocytosis, meropenem started. Bronched, BAL sent. 3/6- Failed SBT, enteral sedation increased. 3/7 Extubated to HFNC 60L/70%. Delirious and combative. Precedex restarted and haldol given w/some improvement. Less alert/arousable 3/8 with equal pupils (5mm) but sluggish responsiveness to light on left. STAT CT head negative for acute abnormality. Lethargic and unresponsive to pain, so Neurology consulted and he was intubated for airway protection. CTA head and neck with no acute process. 1 hr EEG performed with no epileptiform discharges. Lines changed and cx repeated due to persistent leukocytosis. Awake, alert and following commands, moving all 4 extremities on 3/9 but percutaneous tracheostomy per THS team for airway protection and deconditioning. Patient: PARKER, Michael Daniel mrn:a440517097 fin:d4533694142

CVICU Critical Care
50yo obese male with PMH significant for CAD (prior MI s/p pRCA stent-2014), ICM with prior VF arrest (s/p St. Jude ICD), HTN, DM, COPD, OSA, CKD- stage III, persistent afib, pulmonary HTN, depression and liver fibrosis is admitted to cvicu for management of decompensated systolic and diastolic heart failure. He was originally admitted to the hospital 2/15 with decompensated HF and AKI (Cr 2.72 up from baseline ~2). Prior to this, he was last admitted 2021-08-31 - 2021-09-08 with ADHF and was discharged on Milrinone with plan for future LVAD. During that admission, PICC cultured and +Stenotrophomonas and he had a short course of levofloxacin as blood culture negative and did not appear ill. LVAD implantation planned for 2/22 but cancelled due to worsening renal function. He was transferred to CVICU for SGC and possible IABP placement in attempts to medically optimize. Attempted left femoral access for IABP without success. RIJ MAC +PA catheter placed and mixed venous 64%, CVP 6, CI 2.4, PAP 46/26, SVR 1064 on Milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Diuresis held. 2/24 to OR for HM3 LVAD placement. Easy airway. Intraop TEE showed severely enlarged RV w/low normal function and mild TR. Product in OR: 2FFP, 1PLT, 1 CRYO, 2PRBC and 500mL cell-saved blood. Arrived to CVICU on iFlo, Epi, Milrinone, sedated with propofol. Subsequently added fentanyl. PAP's 60/30's, CO/CI 7/3.3, 5LPM flow on LVAD @5600RPM - increased to 5800 in CVICU by MSS. Started on amio that night for AF/RVR. Flolan off 2/25 and epi weaned. UOP and CI declined and CVP rose to ~20. Bedside TTE performed and showed severely enlarged RV w/leftward bowing of interventricular septum. D/w CVS, and reduced RPM to 5600 + epi increased. CVICU Critical Care
50yo obese male with PMH significant for CAD (prior MI s/p pRCA stent-2014), ICM with prior VF arrest (s/p St. Jude ICD), HTN, DM, COPD, OSA, CKD- stage III, persistent afib, pulmonary HTN, depression and liver fibrosis is admitted to cvicu for management of decompensated systolic and diastolic heart failure. He was originally admitted to the hospital 2/15 with decompensated HF and AKI (Cr 2.72 up from baseline ~2). Prior to this, he was last admitted 2021-08-31 - 2021-09-08 with ADHF and was discharged on Milrinone with plan for future LVAD. During that admission, PICC cultured and +Stenotrophomonas and he had a short course of levofloxacin as blood culture negative and did not appear ill. LVAD implantation planned for 2/22 but cancelled due to worsening renal function. He was transferred to CVICU for SGC and possible IABP placement in attempts to medically optimize. Attempted left femoral access for IABP without success. RIJ MAC +PA catheter placed and mixed venous 64%, CVP 6, CI 2.4, PAP 46/26, SVR 1064 on Milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Diuresis held. 2/24 to OR for HM3 LVAD placement. Easy airway. Intraop TEE showed severely enlarged RV w/low normal function and mild TR. Product in OR: 2FFP, 1PLT, 1 CRYO, 2PRBC and 500mL cell-saved blood. Arrived to CVICU on iFlo, Epi, Milrinone, sedated with propofol. Subsequently added fentanyl. PAP's 60/30's, CO/CI 7/3.3, 5LPM flow on LVAD @5600RPM - increased to 5800 in CVICU by MSS. Started on amio that night for AF/RVR. Flolan off 2/25 and epi weaned. UOP and CI declined and CVP rose to ~20. Bedside TTE performed and showed severely enlarged RV w/leftward bowing of interventricular septum. D/w CVS, and reduced RPM to 5600 + epi increased. Additionally, bolused w/Bumex + Diuril. Flolan restarted early 2/26 due to PH + marginal LVAD flow. Repeat bedside TTE on 2/26 with midline septum and dilated LV. LVAD speed increased to 6000 and MAP goal 65-75 with improvement in LVAD flow to >5 LPM. Systemic heparin started. Nephrology consulted 2/27 due to worsening AKI on CKD. Had 2 episodes of increased WOB + poor vent synchrony + poor lung compliance 2/27 that required chemical paralysis. 2/28 Vent dyssynchrony, ETT advancement with continued dyssynchrony and poor compliance. Emergently bronch'd (no obstruction but RLL secretions lavaged/suctioned). Cisatracurium gtt started. CVICU Critical Care
Michael Parker is a 50 y/o white male with past medical history significant for ICM, ICD (St. Jude) with prior VF arrest, CAD-prior MI with proximal RCA stent-2014, HTN, DM, COPD, OSA, CKD- stage III, Persistent Afib, Obesity, class II, Pulm HTN, Depression, and Liver fibrosis. He was admitted on 2/15 with elevated creatinine (2.72)-(baseline ~2). He was last admitted 12/31 through 2021-09-08 with ADHF. He was found to be bacteremic (2/2 PICC, line +stenotrophomonas maltophila). He was eventually discharged home on milrinone. LVAD implant cancelled 2/22 due to worsening renal function. Transferred to CVICU for SGC and possible IABP placement in attempts to medically optimize. Attempted left femoral perc. IABP placement without success. RIJ MAC +PAC obtained with mixed venous 64, CVP 6, CI 2.4, PAP 46/26, SVR 1064 on Milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Diuresis held. 2/24 to OR for HM3 LVAD placement, easy airway. Intraop TEE showed RV severely enlarged w/low normal function and mild TR. Product in OR 2FFP, 1PLT, 1 CRYO, 2Units PRBC while on bypass, 500 CS. Arrived to CVICU on iFlo, Epi, Milrinone, ppf gtt. Subsequently added fentanyl. PAP's 60/30's, CO/CI 7/3.3, 5LPM flow on LVAD @5600RPM - increased to 5800 in CVICU by MSS. 2/25: Started on amio overnight for AF/RVR. Flolan weaned off through the day and epi down to 0.01. Milrinone continued. Through the afternoon, UOP and CI declined to borderline levels and CVP rose to ~20. Bedside TTE performed and showed severely enlarged RV w/leftward bowing of interventricular septum. D/w CVS, and reduced RPM to 5600 + epi dosage increased. Additionally, bolused w/Bumex + Diuril. On repeat examination, septum still bowing to left, but improved from prior. Flolan restarted early 2/26 due to pHTN + falling LVAD flow. Repeat bedside TTE on 2/26 with septum midline and increase in LV size. LVAD speed increased to 6000 with improvement in LVAD flow to >5 LPM. MAP goal 65-75 to facilitate LVAD flow. Systemic heparin started. Nephrology consulted 2/27 due to worsening AKI on CKD. Had 2 episodes of increased WOB + poor vent synchrony + poor tidal volumes 2/27. Required boluses of chemical paralysis. 2/28 Vent dysynchrony, ETT advancement with subsequent decrease in tidal volumes and continued vent dysynchrony resulting in emergent bedside bronch (note contains further details). Cisatracurium gtt started. Amio gtt changed to PO to decrease volume given, NaHCO3 changed to IV push PRN and PO. Given respiratory issues COVID 19 testing done (negative result). 3/1: Paralytic dc'd, changed sedation to hydromorphone and PPF. Weaning Epi gtt as tolerated. Isordil added (later on isordil/hydral). Solumedrol scheduled for PMH of COPD exacerbations. 3/2: iFlo weanted to 0.02. UOP decreased <100ml/hr. Pt hemodynamics did not tolerate weaning. Bedside ECHO done in afternoon revealing poor RV function and nonvariable IVC, CW volume overload. Flolan -> 0.05, milrinone -> 0.375. 3/3 right femoral trialysis placed for HD. 3/4 tolerated PSV but did not pass SBT for extubation. Tolerated dialysis. 3/5- HD with 2L volume removal and subsequent hypotension which resolved with volume replacement. ID consulted for assistance with abx therapy. Patient bronched and BAL sent. Merrem started. 3/6- Failed SBT. Enteral sedation increased. 3/7 Extubated early morning to HFNC 60L/70%. Delirious and combative. Precedex restarted and haldol given w/some improvement. BAL resulted with gram positive cocci and gram neg rods, continue merrem and await speciation. 3/8 - Patient was less arousable this morning. His left eye was dilated (5mm) and sluggish while his right eye was dilated (5mm) and responsive to light. He had STAT CT head which was normal. On return from CT scanner, he was lethargic and would not withdraw to painful stimuli. Neurology was consulted. He was intubated for airway protection. CTA head and neck with no acute process. 1 hr EEG performed with no epileptiform discharges. Lines changed and cx repeated due to persistent leukocytosis. 3/9: He was awake, alert and following commands moving all 4 extremities. Patient had bedside percutaneous tracheostomy with thoracic surgery. 3/10: Patient having bleeding around the trach. The heparin drip was held. The bleeding was controlled with suture, Surgicel and silver nitrate. Continuing to hold heparin.
3/12: Overnight events reviewed. He had 8 beat run of v-tach overnight. His potassium was repleted. He was restarted on nicardipine yesterday. His hydralazine dose was increased and ISDN frequency increased today. Transitioning off insulin drip to Lantus 20u BID and regular insulin 10u q6h + SSI. Received 1u PRBC yesterday. No bleeding noted overnight. Started on Eliquis today. Tolerated iHD (3L). Paced via PPM. He remains supported on LVAD 6000/5.3LPM/4.8W/3.4PI. He continues on milrinone at 0.375 for RV support. He is awake, alert, and moving all extremities. He was transitioned to trach collar and tolerated it for 3 hours. He coughed up well formed old appearing blood clots when switched to pressure support. He was transitioned back to PS 8/8. Tube feeds at goal. Worked with PT.

CVICU Critical Care
Michael Parker is a 50 y/o white male with past medical history significant for ICM, ICD (St. Jude) with prior VF arrest, CAD-prior MI with proximal RCA stent-2014, HTN, DM, COPD, OSA, CKD- stage III, Persistent Afib, Obesity, class II, Pulm HTN, Depression, and Liver fibrosis. He was admitted on 2/15 with elevated creatinine (2.72)-(baseline ~2). He was last admitted 12/31 through 2021-09-08 with ADHF. He was found to be bacteremic (2/2 PICC, line +stenotrophomonas maltophila). He was eventually discharged home on milrinone. LVAD implant cancelled 2/22 due to worsening renal function. Transferred to CVICU for SGC and possible IABP placement in attempts to medically optimize. Attempted left femoral perc. IABP placement without success. RIJ MAC +PAC obtained with mixed venous 64, CVP 6, CI 2.4, PAP 46/26, SVR 1064 on Milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Diuresis held. 2/24 to OR for HM3 LVAD placement, easy airway. Intraop TEE showed RV severely enlarged w/low normal function and mild TR. Product in OR 2FFP, 1PLT, 1 CRYO, 2Units PRBC while on bypass, 500 CS. Arrived to CVICU on iFlo, Epi, Milrinone, ppf gtt. Subsequently added fentanyl. PAP's 60/30's, CO/CI 7/3.3, 5LPM flow on LVAD @5600RPM - increased to 5800 in CVICU by MSS. 2/25: Started on amio overnight for AF/RVR. Flolan weaned off through the day and epi down to 0.01. Milrinone continued. Through the afternoon, UOP and CI declined to borderline levels and CVP rose to ~20. Bedside TTE performed and showed severely enlarged RV w/leftward bowing of interventricular septum. D/w CVS, and reduced RPM to 5600 + epi dosage increased. Additionally, bolused w/Bumex + Diuril. On repeat examination, septum still bowing to left, but improved from prior. Flolan restarted early 2/26 due to pHTN + falling LVAD flow. Repeat bedside TTE on 2/26 with septum midline and increase in LV size. LVAD speed increased to 6000 with improvement in LVAD flow to >5 LPM. MAP goal 65-75 to facilitate LVAD flow. Systemic heparin started. Nephrology consulted 2/27 due to worsening AKI on CKD. Had 2 episodes of increased WOB + poor vent synchrony + poor tidal volumes 2/27. Required boluses of chemical paralysis. 2/28 Vent dysynchrony, ETT advancement with subsequent decrease in tidal volumes and continued vent dysynchrony resulting in emergent bedside bronch (note contains further details). Cisatracurium gtt started. Amio gtt changed to PO to decrease volume given, NaHCO3 changed to IV push PRN and PO. Given respiratory issues COVID 19 testing done (negative result). 3/1: Paralytic dc'd, changed sedation to hydromorphone and PPF. Weaning Epi gtt as tolerated. Isordil added (later on isordil/hydral). Solumedrol scheduled for PMH of COPD exacerbations. 3/2: iFlo weanted to 0.02. UOP decreased <100ml/hr. Pt hemodynamics did not tolerate weaning. Bedside ECHO done in afternoon revealing poor RV function and nonvariable IVC, CW volume overload. Flolan -> 0.05, milrinone -> 0.375. 3/3 right femoral trialysis placed for HD. 3/4 tolerated PSV but did not pass SBT for extubation. Tolerated dialysis. 3/5- HD with 2L volume removal and subsequent hypotension which resolved with volume replacement. ID consulted for assistance with abx therapy. Patient bronched and BAL sent. Merrem started. 3/6- Failed SBT. Enteral sedation increased. 3/7 Extubated early morning to HFNC 60L/70%. Delirious and combative. Precedex restarted and haldol given w/some improvement. BAL resulted with gram positive cocci and gram neg rods, continue merrem and await speciation. 3/8 - Patient was less arousable this morning. His left eye was dilated (5mm) and sluggish while his right eye was dilated (5mm) and responsive to light. He had STAT CT head which was normal. On return from CT scanner, he was lethargic and would not withdraw to painful stimuli. Neurology was consulted. He was intubated for airway protection. CTA head and neck with no acute process. 1 hr EEG performed with no epileptiform discharges. Lines changed and cx repeated due to persistent leukocytosis. 3/9: He was awake, alert and following commands moving all 4 extremities. Patient had bedside percutaneous tracheostomy with thoracic surgery. 3/10: Patient having bleeding around the trach. The heparin drip was held. The bleeding was controlled with suture, Surgicel and silver nitrate. Continuing to hold heparin.
3/11 - Overnight events reviewed. He was initiated on insulin drip for hyperglycemia. He received 1u PRBC overnight along with 12.5g of 5% albumin for anemia + low PI on LVAD. He achieved hemostasis yesterday after the tracheal bleeding area was sutured. No bleeding overnight. Will consider restarting heparin tomorrow. He was transitioned to pressure support 8 and PEEP 8 this morning. Monitoring for tolerance. Working to optimize respiratory status. Paced via PPM. He remains supported on LVAD 6000/5.6LPM/4.8W/1.7PI. He continues on milrinone at 0.375 for RV support. His Cardene was weaned off after starting ISDN. He is to receive 1u PRBC today for anemia. He had 5 loose BMs over the last 24 hours. His bowel regimen was discontinued today. He worked with therapy and was able to sit at the side of the bed. Transfer to cardiac chair today. He is awake, interactive and MAE.

Title: Arterial Line Procedure Note
Author: SHUFFITT, CHERYL L, APRN-PUL

Patient: PARKER, Michael Daniel mrn:a440517097 fin:d4533694142
Age: 50 Years Sex: Male DOB: 1970-12-03

INDICATION: Continuous BP monitoring, vasoactive drug titration
PROCEDURE OPERATOR: Cheryl Shuffitt, APRN
PROCEDURE SUMMARY:
A time out was performed. My hands were washed immediately prior to the procedure. I wore a surgical cap, mask with protective eyewear, sterile gown and sterile gloves throughout the procedure. The right arm was prepped using chlorhexidine scrub and draped in sterile fashion using a three quarter sheet drape and sterile towels. The brachial pulse was identified by ultrasound. Anesthesia was achieved using 1% lidocaine. Using out of plane ultrasound guidance, a needle attached to a syringe, was inserted into the brachial artery with constant negative aspiration pressure. Arterial blood was seen to pulsate in the syringe. The syringe was removed and a guidewire was advanced easily into the brachial artery. The catheter was then advanced over the wire and the needle and wire were withdrawn. The catheter was sutured in place. A sterile opsite was placed over the catheter at the insertion site. The patient tolerated the procedure without any hemodynamic compromise. At the time of procedure completion, the catheter was connected to the cardiac monitor and calibrated. Appropriate waveform and blood pressure tracing was observed. Estimated blood loss is 5cc
Cheryl Shuffitt, APRN

CVICU Critical Care
Michael Parker is a 50 y/o white male with past medical history significant for ICM, ICD (St. Jude) with prior VF arrest, CAD-prior MI with proximal RCA stent-2014, HTN, DM, COPD, OSA, CKD- stage III, Persistent Afib, Obesity, class II, Pulm HTN, Depression, and Liver fibrosis. He was admitted on 2/15 with elevated creatinine (2.72)-(baseline ~2). He was last admitted 12/31 through 2021-09-08 with ADHF. He was found to be bacteremic (2/2 PICC, line +stenotrophomonas maltophila). He was eventually discharged home on milrinone. LVAD implant cancelled 2/22 due to worsening renal function. Transferred to CVICU for SGC and possible IABP placement in attempts to medically optimize. Attempted left femoral perc. IABP placement without success. RIJ MAC +PAC obtained with mixed venous 64, CVP 6, CI 2.4, PAP 46/26, SVR 1064 on Milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Diuresis held. 2/24 to OR for HM3 LVAD placement, easy airway. Intraop TEE showed RV severely enlarged w/low normal function and mild TR. Product in OR 2FFP, 1PLT, 1 CRYO, 2Units PRBC while on bypass, 500 CS. Arrived to CVICU on iFlo, Epi, Milrinone, ppf gtt subsequently added fentanyl. Elevated PAP's 60/30's, CO/CI 7/3.3 5L flow on LVAD @5600RPM increased to 5800 in CVICU by MSS. 2/25: Started on amio overnight for AF/RVR. Flolan weaned off through the day and epi down to 0.01. Milrinone continued. Through the afternoon, UOP and CI declined to borderline levels and CVP rose to ~20. Bedside TTE performed and showed severely enlarged RV w/leftward bowing of interventricular septum. D/w CVS, and reduced RPM to 5600 + epi dosage increased. Additionally, bolused w/Bumex + Diuril. 2. Congestive Heart Failure s/p LVAD
3. Coronary Artery Disease
POSTTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS:
PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSES:
1. Respiratory failure.
2. Congestive Heart Failure s/p LVAD
3. Coronary Artery Disease
PROCEDURES PERFORMED:
1. Flexible bronchoscopy.
2. Percutaneous tracheostomy.
ASSISTANT:
Neal Bhutiani, M.D.-PGY-5
ANESTHESIA:
General.
TUBES AND DRAINS:
#8 proximal XLT Shiley tracheostomy.
COMPLICATIONS:
None immediate.
ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS:
5 mL.
INDICATIONS FOR PROCEDURE:
50 year old gentleman with history significant for HFrEF (ICM-TTE-11/2020-EF-29%) s/p insertion of HeartMate 3 left ventricular assist device, ligation of left atrial appendage 2021-10-24, CAD s/p MI and PCI to RCA around 2014, HTN, T2DM, COPD and OSA, who thoracic surgery was consulted on tracheostomy. Patient is approximately 2 weeks out from LVAD placement. He was extubated 2021-11-07 and placed on high flow nasal cannula. He had been progressing some; however, this morning patient developed stroke like symptoms and was reintubated for airway protection. CT head negative and neurology workup ongoing. Thoracic surgery was consulted for tracheostomy. Patient currently on 18/500/40/10. Sedated on propofol. It is unlikely that he will be extubated in the near future and would benefit
from a tracheostomy. We were consulted for this procedure. The risks and
benefits were discussed with the patient's brother, Ashley, and consent was obtained.
DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE:
After informed consent was obtained, the patient was identified in the
cardiovascular intensive care unit by the attending surgeon as well as the
anesthesia staff. They were placed flat in the supine position with a shoulder
roll. The bed was inflated. His head was extended to provide better exposure
to the trachea. Once the endoscopy team was on site, a surgical time-out was
performed. Perioperative antibiotics were not indicated. After completion of
a surgical time-out, a Portex adaptor was connected to the pre-existing
endotracheal tube. Flexible bronchoscopy was performed. The scope was
extended out to the subsegmental bronchi. These were normal. There was no
evidence of any endobronchial lesions. There were some thick tenacious secretions. These were evacuated and
a bronchoalveolar lavage was sent from the right middle lobe. At this time, the
endotracheal tube was freed from the tube holder. The balloon was deflated
and the endotracheal tube was pulled back. The patient had previously been
placed on 100% oxygen. The oxygen saturations were adequate. The patient was hemodynamically stable. He did receive
rocuronium, 100 mg, as well as the propofol which he had already been receiving. At this time, the
patient's neck was prepped and draped in normal sterile fashion. A vertical
incision was made approximately 1 fingerbreadth above the sternal notch after instilling with 3 cc of 1% Lidocaine. The soft
tissue was spread using a Kelly clamp. A finder needle was inserted at this
location. We observed the needle traversing between
just below the 3nd tracheal ring. The needle was removed leaving the sheath
in place. A guidewire was advanced under bronchoscopic guidance. The sheath
was removed. A 4 cm 14-French dilator was then inserted. This was removed
leaving guidewire in place. We subsequently followed with the Blue rhino
with a guiding catheter over the guidewire using Seldinger technique. This
was advanced to the level of the black line at the level of the skin. All dilations were
observed under bronchoscopy. The Blue rhino was removed leaving the guiding
catheter in place. A loading dilator was placed on a #8 regular Shiley
tracheostomy. This was advanced over the guidewire engaging the guiding
catheter and advanced as a unit. The trachea was entered without
difficulty under visualization. The loading dilator, guidewire, and guiding
catheter were removed. The bronchoscope was then exchanged from the ET tube
into the tracheostomy. It sat in good position above the carina. The
balloon was inflated. The inner cannula was inserted. The patient was connected
to the ventilator with marginal tidal volumes and adequate CO2 capnography. His oxygen sats were adequate.
The flexible bronchoscope was then placed back through the ET tube. The balloon
was sitting slightly shallow but within the trachea. Given this, I elected to exchange to a #8 proximal XLT Shiley.
The ETT was readvanced. The balloon was deflated on the tracheostomy and the patient was ventilated through the ETT.
The guidewire was readvanced under direct vision with the bronchoscope in the ETT. The tracheostomy was removed and the
guiding catheter and wire were left in place. The #8 proximal XLT was inserted using a loading dilator in the standard fashion.
The guidewire, loading dilator and guiding catheter were all removed. The bronchoscope was placed through the tracheostomy
after the inner cannula was inserted, confirming to be in good position a few centimeters above the carina. Bronchoscopy through
the ETT should the balloon sitting flush against the trachea wall. Completion bronchoscopy was performed through the tracheostomy. There was minimal
bleeding within the airway. Any scant blood was evacuated. The scope was removed. The tidal volumes were still low and the vent was adjusted with
a higher driving pressure with increase in tidal volumes. His sats remained above 95% the entire procedure.
The tracheostomy was secured in place using Prolene sutures on the upper flange. A pink foam was placed
underneath the flange and a trach collar was placed beneath to protect the
underlying skin. This terminated the procedure. The patient remained hemodynamically stable throughout the case. I was the
attending physician. I was present for the entire care. I performed
the bronchoscopic portion. Dr. Bhutiani served as my assistant, performing the tracheostomy insertion.
_____________________________
Matthew Black, M.D.

Title: CVICU Critical Care
Author: CONDLEY, CLAY, MD-ANS

Patient: PARKER, Michael Daniel mrn:a440517097 fin:d4533694142
Age: 50 Years Sex: Male DOB: 1970-12-03

CVICU Critical Care
Michael Parker is a 50 y/o white male with past medical history significant for ICM, ICD (St. Jude) with prior VF arrest, CAD-prior MI with proximal RCA stent-2014, HTN, DM, COPD, OSA, CKD- stage III, Persistent Afib, Obesity, class II, Pulm HTN, Depression, and Liver fibrosis. He was admitted on 2/15 with elevated creatinine (2.72)-(baseline ~2). He was last admitted 12/31 through 2021-09-08 with ADHF. He was found to be bacteremic (2/2 PICC, line +stenotrophomonas maltophila). He was eventually discharged home on milrinone. LVAD implant cancelled 2/22 due to worsening renal function. Transferred to CVICU for SGC and possible IABP placement in attempts to medically optimize. Attempted left femoral perc. IABP placement without success. RIJ MAC +PAC obtained with mixed venous 64, CVP 6, CI 2.4, PAP 46/26, SVR 1064 on Milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Diuresis held. 2/24 to OR for HM3 LVAD placement, easy airway. Intraop TEE showed RV severely enlarged w/low normal function and mild TR. Product in OR 2FFP, 1PLT, 1 CRYO, 2Units PRBC while on bypass, 500 CS. Arrived to CVICU on iFlo, Epi, Milrinone, ppf gtt subsequently added fentanyl. Elevated PAP's 60/30's, CO/CI7/3.3 5L flow on LVAD @5600RPM increased to 5800 in CVICU by MSS. 2/25: Started on amio overnight for AF/RVR. Flolan weaned off through the day and epi down to 0.01. Milrinone continued. Through the afternoon, UOP and CI declined to borderline levels and CVP rose to ~20. Bedside TTE performed and showed severely enlarged RV w/leftward bowing of interventricular septum. D/w CVS, and reduced RPM to 5600 + epi dosage increased. Additionally, bolused w/Bumex + Diuril. On repeat examination, septum still bowing to left, but improved from prior. Flolan restarted early 2/26 due to pHTN + falling LVAD flow. Repeat bedside TTE on 2/26 with septum midline and increase in LV size. LVAD speed increased to 6000 with improvement in LVAD flow to >5 LPM. MAP goal 65-75 to facilitate LVAD flow. Systemic heparin started. Nephrology consulted 2/27 due to worsening AKI on CKD. Had 2 episodes of increased WOB + poor vent synchrony + poor tidal volumes 2/27. Title: CVICU Critical Care Note
Author: CONDLEY, CLAY, MD-ANS

Patient: PARKER, Michael Daniel mrn:a440517097 fin:d4533694142
Age: 50 Years Sex: Male DOB: 1970-12-03

CVICU Critical Care
Michael Parker is a 50 y/o white male with past medical history significant for ICM, ICD (St. Jude) with prior VF arrest, CAD-prior MI with proximal RCA stent-2014, HTN, DM, COPD, OSA, CKD- stage III, Persistent Afib, Obesity, class II, Pulm HTN, Depression, and Liver fibrosis. He was admitted on 2/15 with elevated creatinine (2.72)-(baseline ~2). He was last admitted 12/31 through 2021-09-08 with ADHF. He was found to be bacteremic (2/2 PICC, line +stenotrophomonas maltophila). He was eventually discharged home on milrinone. LVAD implant cancelled 2/22 due to worsening renal function. Transferred to CVICU for SGC and possible IABP placement in attempts to medically optimize. Attempted left femoral perc. IABP placement without success. RIJ MAC +PAC obtained with mixed venous 64, CVP 6, CI 2.4, PAP 46/26, SVR 1064 on Milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Diuresis held. 2/24 to OR for HM3 LVAD placement, easy airway. Intraop TEE showed RV severely enlarged w/low normal function and mild TR. Product in OR 2FFP, 1PLT, 1 CRYO, 2Units PRBC while on bypass, 500 CS. Arrived to CVICU on iFlo, Epi, Milrinone, ppf gtt subsequently added fentanyl. Elevated PAP's 60/30's, CO/CI7/3.3 5L flow on LVAD @5600RPM increased to 5800 in CVICU by MSS. 2/25: Started on amio overnight for AF/RVR. Flolan weaned off through the day and epi down to 0.01. Milrinone continued. Through the afternoon, UOP and CI declined to borderline levels and CVP rose to ~20. Bedside TTE performed and showed severely enlarged RV w/leftward bowing of interventricular septum. D/w CVS, and reduced RPM to 5600 + epi dosage increased. Additionally, bolused w/Bumex + Diuril. On repeat examination, septum still bowing to left, but improved from prior. Flolan restarted early 2/26 due to pHTN + falling LVAD flow. Repeat bedside TTE on 2/26 with septum midline and increase in LV size. LVAD speed increased to 6000 with improvement in LVAD flow to >5 LPM. MAP goal 65-75 to facilitate LVAD flow. Systemic heparin started. Nephrology consulted 2/27 due to worsening AKI on CKD. Had 2 episodes of increased WOB + poor vent synchrony + poor tidal volumes 2/27. Required boluses of chemical paralysis. 2/28 Vent dysynchrony, ETT advancement with subsequent decrease in tidal volumes and continued vent dysynchrony resulting in emergent bedside bronch (note contains further details), bronch culture pending. Cisatracurium gtt started. Amio gtt changed to PO to decrease volume given, NaHCO3 changed to IV push PRN and PO. Given respiratory issues COVID 19 testing done (negative result). 3/1: NAEON. Paralytic dc'd, changed sedation to hydromorphone and PPF. Weaning Epi gtt as tolerated, Isordil added. Aggressive diuresing r/t continued positived IO balance, Bumex gtt increased, Diuril scheduled doses. Vent settings tailored for patient increased PEEP to 12 and Fi02 50%, solumedrol scheduled doses for PMH of COPD exacerbations. AM increased residuals, TF held. LVAD settings: 6000 RPM, 5.5 LPM, 3.8 PI, 4.9 W Power. Vent settings: PRVC RR20, V450, 12 PEEP, FiO2 50%. Overnight elevated BHOB and glucoses D10 and insulin gtts restarted. 3/2: Weaning sedation as tolerated with aims towards extubation, patient opens eyes and follows commands. Pt had multiple episodes of HTN Isordil and hydralazine doses subsequently increased +PRN hydral doses added for map goal of 75. iFlo weanted to 0.02 UOP decreased <100ml/hr pt hemodynamics did not tolerate weaning, bedside ECHO done in afternoon revealing poor RV function nonvariable IVC CW volume overload Flolan increased back to 0.05 milrinone 0.375. Ventilator settings optimized for patient requirements PC 18/IP15/+5/40%, MCT and PCT removed. Mr Parker is a 50 year old male needing bronchoscopy due to elevated peak pressures and respiratory distress. Informed consent obtained. Bedside timeout performed. Cap, mask, sterile gloves donned. Patient placed on 100% O2. Sedation with: existing sedative infusions. Fiberoptic bronchoscope passed easily through and bronchial tree inspected bilaterally. Findings included: copious purulent secretions through proximal airway and into RML and RLL. Erythematous, collapsible mucosa. Fluid instilled: 50cc sterile saline for BAL. BAL: RML, 50cc sterile saline instilled and 10cc returned. Bronchoscope removed from airway. Patient tolerated the procedure well without apparent complications.

CVICU Critical Care
Michael Parker is a 50 y/o white male with past medical history significant for ICM, ICD (St. Jude) with prior VF arrest, CAD-prior MI with proximal RCA stent-2014, HTN, DM, COPD, OSA, CKD- stage III, Persistent Afib, Obesity, class II, Pulm HTN, Depression, and Liver fibrosis. He was admitted on 2/15 with elevated creatinine (2.72)-(baseline ~2). He was last admitted 12/31 through 2021-09-08 with ADHF. He was found to be bacteremic (2/2 PICC, line +stenotrophomonas maltophila). He was eventually discharged home on milrinone. LVAD implant cancelled 2/22 due to worsening renal function. Transferred to CVICU for SGC and possible IABP placement in attempts to medically optimize. Attempted left femoral perc. IABP placement without success. RIJ MAC +PAC obtained with mixed venous 64, CVP 6, CI 2.4, PAP 46/26, SVR 1064 on Milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Diuresis held. 2/24 to OR for HM3 LVAD placement, easy airway. Intraop TEE showed RV severely enlarged w/low normal function and mild TR. Product in OR 2FFP, 1PLT, 1 CRYO, 2Units PRBC while on bypass, 500 CS. Arrived to CVICU on iFlo, Epi, Milrinone, ppf gtt subsequently added fentanyl. Elevated PAP's 60/30's, CO/CI7/3.3 5L flow on LVAD @5600RPM increased to 5800 in CVICU by MSS. 2/25: Started on amio overnight for AF/RVR. Flolan weaned off through the day and epi down to 0.01. Milrinone continued. Through the afternoon, UOP and CI declined to borderline levels and CVP rose to ~20. Bedside TTE performed and showed severely enlarged RV w/leftward bowing of interventricular septum. D/w CVS, and reduced RPM to 5600 + epi dosage increased. Additionally, bolused w/Bumex + Diuril. On repeat examination, septum still bowing to left, but improved from prior. Flolan restarted early 2/26 due to pHTN + falling LVAD flow. Repeat bedside TTE on 2/26 with septum midline and increase in LV size. LVAD speed increased to 6000 with improvement in LVAD flow to >5 LPM. MAP goal 65-75 to facilitate LVAD flow. Systemic heparin started. Nephrology consulted 2/27 due to worsening AKI on CKD. Had 2 episodes of increased WOB + poor vent synchrony + poor tidal volumes 2/27. Required boluses of chemical paralysis. 2/28 Vent dysynchrony, ETT advancement with subsequent decrease in tidal volumes and continued vent dysynchrony resulting in emergent bedside bronch (note contains further details), bronch culture pending. Cisatracurium gtt started. Amio gtt changed to PO to decrease volume given, NaHCO3 changed to IV push PRN and PO. Given respiratory issues COVID 19 testing done (negative result). 3/1: NAEON. Paralytic dc'd, changed sedation to hydromorphone and PPF. Weaning Epi gtt as tolerated, Isordil added. Aggressive diuresing r/t continued positived IO balance, Bumex gtt increased, Diuril scheduled doses. Vent settings tailored for patient increased PEEP to 12 and Fi02 50%, solumedrol scheduled doses for PMH of COPD exacerbations. AM increased residuals, TF held. LVAD settings: 6000 RPM, 5.5 LPM, 3.8 PI, 4.9 W Power. Vent settings: PRVC RR20, V450, 12 PEEP, FiO2 50%. Overnight elevated BHOB and glucoses D10 and insulin gtts restarted. 3/2: Weaning sedation as tolerated with aims towards extubation, patient opens eyes and follows commands. Pt had multiple episodes of HTN Isordil and hydralazine doses subsequently increased +PRN hydral doses added for map goal of 75. iFlo weanted to 0.02 UOP decreased <100ml/hr pt hemodynamics did not tolerate weaning, bedside ECHO done in afternoon revealing poor RV function nonvariable IVC CW volume overload Flolan increased back to 0.05 milrinone 0.375. Ventilator settings optimized for patient requirements PC 18/IP15/+5/40%, MCT and PCT removed. Continuing to diurese on bumex gtt and q6 diuril with goal to net negative 3L, lytes being repleted as necessary. No BM since prior to OR Relistor added to bowel reg. Elevated BHOB and glucoses overnight continuing D10 and insulin gtt. Remains afebrile, BAL from 2/28 NGTD. Overnight had x1 episode of vent dysynchony which required x1 dose of midaz and 1 dose of Roc, 3% metanebs were added. Some PAC's overnight not requiring amio bolus or further intervention, CI 3.5 which prompted a decrease in iFlo to 0.04. X3 BM overnight once relistor added yesterday.
3/3: Sedation increased to allow for patient comfort and vent dysynchrony overnight. VAD flows 5.5/6000/pi41/+4.9 LDH 202, 2D Echo done to assess IVC, Inflow and outflow status. PAP's 33/15(21) CVP 11, maintaining CI >2.5, attempted to wean flolan yesterday but increasing CVP,PAP's, and dropping UOP prompted increase back to 0.05, plan is to attempt to wean today. Tolerating current ventilator settings without evidence of dysynchrony changed back to PC 18/12/+12/40% with appropriate vT, cngestion on the right side, suctioning PRN +secretions, sending sputum cx. Bumex gtt dc'd, continuing diuril q12, Right femoral Trialysis catheter placed for HD per nephrology. Continues to make UOP 3.6L x24hrs however his overall balance remains positive. WBC stable at 13 CRP elevated (62) will send blood/sputum/UA/repeat covid19. Tolerating TF currently on Nepro at 20ml/hr stooling after Relistor given 3/2, Nutrition recs continuous enteral feeds with Vital HP @ 10 mL/hr adv 10 mL Q6 as tolerated to goal 70 mL/hr however pt going on CRRT requirements may change follow-up assessment tomorrow. CVICU Critical Care
Michael Parker is a 50 y/o white male with past medical history significant for ICM, ICD (St. Jude) with prior VF arrest, CAD-prior MI with proximal RCA stent-2014, HTN, DM, COPD, OSA, CKD- stage III, Persistent Afib, Obesity, class II, Pulm HTN, Depression, and Liver fibrosis. He was admitted on 2/15 with elevated creatinine (2.72)-(baseline ~2). He was last admitted 12/31 through 2021-09-08 with ADHF. He was found to be bacteremic (2/2 PICC, line +stenotrophomonas maltophila). He was eventually discharged home on milrinone. LVAD implant cancelled 2/22 due to worsening renal function. Transferred to CVICU for SGC and possible IABP placement in attempts to medically optimize. Attempted left femoral perc. IABP placement without success. RIJ MAC +PAC obtained with mixed venous 64, CVP 6, CI 2.4, PAP 46/26, SVR 1064 on Milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Diuresis held. 2/24 to OR for HM3 LVAD placement, easy airway. Intraop TEE showed RV severely enlarged w/low normal function and mild TR. Product in OR 2FFP, 1PLT, 1 CRYO, 2Units PRBC while on bypass, 500 CS. Arrived to CVICU on iFlo, Epi, Milrinone, ppf gtt subsequently added fentanyl. Elevated PAP's 60/30's, CO/CI7/3.3 5L flow on LVAD @5600RPM increased to 5800 in CVICU by MSS. 2/25: Started on amio overnight for AF/RVR. Flolan weaned off through the day and epi down to 0.01. Milrinone continued. Through the afternoon, UOP and CI declined to borderline levels and CVP rose to ~20. Bedside TTE performed and showed severely enlarged RV w/leftward bowing of interventricular septum. D/w CVS, and reduced RPM to 5600 + epi dosage increased. Additionally, bolused w/Bumex + Diuril. On repeat examination, septum still bowing to left, but improved from prior. Flolan restarted early 2/26 due to pHTN + falling LVAD flow. Repeat bedside TTE on 2/26 with septum midline and increase in LV size. LVAD speed increased to 6000 with improvement in LVAD flow to >5 LPM. MAP goal 65-75 to facilitate LVAD flow. Systemic heparin started. Nephrology consulted 2/27 due to worsening AKI on CKD. Had 2 episodes of increased WOB + poor vent synchrony + poor tidal volumes 2/27. Required boluses of chemical paralysis. 2/28 Vent dysynchrony, ETT advancement with subsequent decrease in tidal volumes and continued vent dysynchrony resulting in emergent bedside bronch (note contains further details), bronch culture pending. Cisatracurium gtt started. Amio gtt changed to PO to decrease volume given, NaHCO3 changed to IV push PRN and PO. Given respiratory issues COVID 19 testing done (negative result).
3/1: NAEON. Paralytic dc'd, changed sedation to hydromorphone and PPF. Weaning Epi gtt as tolerated, Isordil added. Aggressive diuresing r/t continued positived IO balance Bumex gtt increased, Diuril scheduled doses. Vent settings tailored for patient increased PEEP to 12 and Fi02 50%, solumedrol scheduled doses for PMH of COPD exacerbations. AM increased residuals, TF held. LVAD settings: 6000 RPM, 5.5 LPM, 3.8 PI, 4.9 W Power. Vent settings: PRVC RR20, V450, 12 PEEP, FiO2 50%

He was admitted on 2/15 with elevated creatinine (2.72)-(baseline ~2). He was last admitted 12/31 through 2021-09-08 with ADHF. He was found to be bacteremic (2/2 PICC, line +stenotrophomonas maltophila). He was eventually discharged home on milrinone. LVAD implant cancelled 2/22 due to worsening renal function. Transferred to CVICU for SGC and possible IABP placement in attempts to medically optimize. Attempted left femoral perc. IABP placement without success. RIJ MAC +PAC obtained with mixed venous 64, CVP 6, CI 2.4, PAP 46/26, SVR 1064 on Milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min. Diuresis held. 2/24 to OR for HM3 LVAD placement, easy airway. Intraop TEE showed RV severely enlarged w/low normal function and mild TR. Product in OR 2FFP, 1PLT, 1 CRYO, 2Units PRBC while on bypass, 500 CS. Arrived to CVICU on iFlo, Epi, Milrinone, ppf gtt subsequently added fentanyl. Elevated PAP's 60/30's, CO/CI7/3.3 5L flow on LVAD @5600RPM increased to 5800 in CVICU by MSS. 2/25: Started on amio overnight for AF/RVR. Flolan weaned off through the day and epi down to 0.01. Milrinone continued. Through the afternoon, UOP and CI declined to borderline levels and CVP rose to ~20. Bedside TTE performed and showed severely enlarged RV w/leftward bowing of interventricular septum. D/w CVS, and reduced RPM to 5600 + epi dosage increased. Additionally, bolused w/Bumex + Diuril. On repeat examination, septum still bowing to left, but improved from prior. Flolan restarted early 2/26 due to pHTN + falling LVAD flow. Repeat bedside TTE on 2/26 with septum midline and increase in LV size. LVAD speed increased to 6000 with improvement in LVAD flow to >5 LPM. MAP goal 65-75 to facilitate LVAD flow. Systemic heparin started. Nephrology consulted 2/27 due to worsening AKI on CKD. Had 2 episodes of increased WOB + poor vent synchrony + poor tidal volumes 2/27. Required boluses of chemical paralysis.
2/28: Overnight patient had more episodes of vent dyssynchrony requiring paralysis as sedation boluses did not fix the issue. During these events, patient was tachypneic. This AM patient had another episode with decrease tidal volumes, desaturation, and vent dyssynchrony which happened after the ETT was advanced by 2 cm to 28 (as high riding on CXR). Emergent bronch was performed (see separate note for further details). ETT position was optimized under direct visualization. Given dyssynchrony, started on cisatracurium drip. Continuing sedation regimen. Monitoring BIS and TOF twitches. Keeping inotropes as is. Switching amiodarone drip to PO in order to decrease overall volume given. Vent setting switched to PRVC RR26, VT450, PEEP9, FiO2 100->60%. Inhaled flolan back up to 0.05. On exam, diminished course crackly wheezy breathing sounds. On XR, pulmonary edema present. Discussed with Nephrology. Bumex infusion started and diuril given. Bicarb infusion to PO + pushes as needed. Increasing Nepro to 30. Adding linaclotide. Continue insulin drip. Continue heparin drip. Given acute respiratory issues, COVID test was sent (resulted negative). Bronch culture pending.

POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSES: Same

DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE: Procedure done emergently due to patient distress. Monitors in place. Sedation was achieved with existing drips. Rocuronium 50mg given. The patient was placed on controlled ventilation with 100% FiO2. At this point, a fiber optic bronchoscope was inserted into the endotracheal tube. ETT position optimized at 26 cm at lip (~2cm above carina). Systematic inspection was then carried out of the entire tracheobronchial tree. Minimal mucoid and mucosanguineous secretions were suctioned and cleared - most prominent at RLL orifice. The bronchoscope was then removed and cleared of proximal airway debris. A suction trap was installed in line and the scope was reinserted and advanced to the [right lower] lobe and the bronchoscope was wedged into a [basal] segment. Bronchoalveolar lavage was then performed at this segment utilizing 30 mL of saline.
Chest X-Cindy was ordered to evaluate for pneumothorax.
FINDINGS: Upon lavage of the [right lower] lobes, there was aspiration of mucoid and mucosanguineous secretions. These [cleared] after suctioning and lavage.
I was present throughout the procedure. Patient tolerated the procedure well with no apparent complications.

Procedure: Right IJ MAC +PAC
Consent obtained from patient. Hat/mask applied. Right neck prepped with chlor. scrub. Sterile gown and double gloves
applied. Sterile drape applied. R neck anesthesized with 1% lidocaine. R IJ accessed via US guidance. Wire
threaded easily. Needle removed. Catheter threaded over wire. Manometry consistent with venous stick.
Wire reinserted. Skin nick made. MAC cordis advanced over wire easily. Wire and dilator removed. Secured with
suture. All ports aspirated and flushed easily. tolerated well. Next, outer gloves were removed. sterile drape applied
over medial cordis port. PA catheter brought into sterile field. All ports flushed. Swan inserted
to 25 cm. Balloon inflated. PA cath advanced RV and then into pulm artery. Appropriate waveforms obtained on monitor.
Catheter secured at 50 cm. Tolerated well. PCXR ordered.

Fluid Restriction
With some health conditions, you must restrict your fluid intake. This means that you need to limit the amount of fluid that you drink each day (fluid restriction). When you have a fluid restriction, you must carefully measure and keep track of the amount of fluid that you drink. Your health care provider will identify the specific amount of fluid you are allowed each day (fluid allowance). This amount may depend on several things, such as:
• How well your kidneys function.
• How much fluid you are keeping (retaining) in your body tissues.
• Your blood pressure.
• Your heart function.
• Your blood sodium level.
What is my plan?
Your health care provider recommends that you limit your fluid intake to __________ per day.
What counts toward my fluid intake?
Your fluid intake includes all liquids that you drink, as well as any foods that become liquid at room temperature.
The following are examples of some fluids that you will have to restrict:
• Tea, coffee, soda, lemonade, milk, water, juice, sports drinks, and nutritional supplement beverages.
• Alcoholic beverages.
• Cream.
• Gravy.
• Ice cubes.
• Soup and broth.
The following are examples of foods that become liquid at room temperature. These foods will also count toward your fluid intake.
• Ice cream and ice milk.
• Frozen yogurt and sherbet.
• Frozen ice pops.
• Flavored gelatin.
How do I keep track of my fluid intake?
Each morning, fill a jug with the amount of water that is equal to your daily fluid allowance. You can use this water as a guideline for fluid allowance. Each time you take in any form of fluid (including ice cubes and foods that become liquid at room temperature), pour an equal amount of water out of the container. This helps you to see how much fluid you are taking in. It also helps you to see how much more fluid you can take in during the rest of the day.
The following conversions may also be helpful in measuring your fluid intake:
• 1 cup equals 8 oz (240 mL).
• ¾ cup equals 6 oz (180 mL).
• ⅔ cup equals 5⅓ oz (160 mL).
• ½ cup equals 4 oz (120 mL).
• ⅓ cup equals 2⅔ oz (80 mL).
• ¼ cup equals 2 oz (60 mL).
• 2 Tbsp equals 1 oz (30 mL).
What are tips for following this plan?
General instructions
• Make sure that you stay within your recommended fluid allowance each day. Always measure and keep track of your fluids (including ice cubes and foods that become liquid at room temperature).
• Use small cups and glasses and learn to sip fluids slowly.
• Try frozen fruits between meals, such as grapes or strawberries. These can satisfy thirst without adding to your fluid intake.
• Swallow your pills along with meals or soft foods such as applesauce or mashed potatoes, instead of with liquids. Doing this helps you to save your fluid allowance for something that you enjoy.
Weigh yourself each day
Weigh yourself every day. Keeping track of your daily weight can help you and your health care provider to notice as soon as possible if you are retaining too much fluid in your body.
• Follow this sequence every morning:
1. Urinate.
2. Weigh yourself.
3. Eat breakfast.
• Wear the same amount of clothing each time you weigh yourself.
• Write down your daily weight. Give this weight record to your health care provider. If your weight is going up, you may be retaining too much fluid. Every 1 lb (0.45 kg) of body weight that you gain is a sign that your body is retaining 2 cups (480 mL) of fluid.
Manage your thirst
• Add lemon juice or a slice of fresh lemon to water or ice. Doing this helps to satisfy your thirst.
• Freeze fruit juice or water in an ice cube tray. Use this as part of your fluid allowance. These cubes are useful for quenching your thirst. Before you freeze the juice or water, measure how much liquid you use to fill a cube section of the ice tray. Subtract this amount from your day's allowance each time you consume a frozen cube.
• Avoid salty (high-sodium) foods. These foods make you thirsty and make it more difficult to stay within your daily fluid allowance.
• Keep the temperature in your home at a cooler level.
• Keep the air in your home as humid as possible. Dry air increases thirst.
• Avoid being out in the hot sun, which can cause you to sweat and become thirsty.
• To help avoid dry mouth, brush your teeth often or rinse out your mouth with mouthwash. Lemon wedges, hard sour candies, chewing gum, or breath spray may also help to moisten your mouth.
What are some signs that I may be taking in too much fluid?
You may be taking in too much fluid if:
• Your weight increases. Contact your health care provider if you gain weight rapidly.
• Your face, hands, legs, feet, and abdomen start to swell.
• You have trouble breathing.
Summary
• With some health conditions, you must limit (restrict) your fluid intake. This means that you need to limit the amount of fluid you drink each day (fluid restriction). Your health care provider will identify the specific amount of fluid that you are allowed each day.
• When you have a fluid restriction, you must carefully measure and keep track of the amount of fluid that you drink.
• Your fluid intake includes all liquids that you drink, as well as any foods that become liquid at room temperature (such as ice cream and gelatin).
• You may be taking in too much fluid if your weight increases, your body starts to swell, or you have trouble breathing.
This information is not intended to replace advice given to you by your health care provider. Make sure you discuss any questions you have with your health care provider.

Heart-Healthy Eating Plan
Many factors influence your heart (coronary) health, including eating and exercise habits. Coronary risk increases with abnormal blood fat (lipid) levels. Heart-healthy meal planning includes limiting unhealthy fats, increasing healthy fats, and making other diet and lifestyle changes.
What is my plan?
Your health care provider may recommend that you:
• Limit your fat intake to _________% or less of your total calories each day.
• Limit your saturated fat intake to _________% or less of your total calories each day.
• Limit the amount of cholesterol in your diet to less than _________ mg per day.
What are tips for following this plan?
Cooking
Cook foods using methods other than frying. Baking, boiling, grilling, and broiling are all good options. Other ways to reduce fat include:
• Removing the skin from poultry.
• Removing all visible fats from meats.
• Steaming vegetables in water or broth.
Meal planning
• At meals, imagine dividing your plate into fourths:
◦ Fill one-half of your plate with vegetables and green salads.
◦ Fill one-fourth of your plate with whole grains.
◦ Fill one-fourth of your plate with lean protein foods.
• Eat 4–5 servings of vegetables per day. One serving equals 1 cup raw or cooked vegetable, or 2 cups raw leafy greens.
• Eat 4–5 servings of fruit per day. One serving equals 1 medium whole fruit, ¼ cup dried fruit, ½ cup fresh, frozen, or canned fruit, or ½ cup 100% fruit juice.
• Eat more foods that contain soluble fiber. Examples include apples, broccoli, carrots, beans, peas, and barley. Aim to get 25–30 g of fiber per day.
• Increase your consumption of legumes, nuts, and seeds to 4–5 servings per week. One serving of dried beans or legumes equals ½ cup cooked, 1 serving of nuts is ¼ cup, and 1 serving of seeds equals 1 tablespoon.
Fats
• Choose healthy fats more often. Choose monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats, such as olive and canola oils, flaxseeds, walnuts, almonds, and seeds.
• Eat more omega-3 fats. Choose salmon, mackerel, sardines, tuna, flaxseed oil, and ground flaxseeds. Aim to eat fish at least 2 times each week.
• Check food labels carefully to identify foods with trans fats or high amounts of saturated fat.
• Limit saturated fats. These are found in animal products, such as meats, butter, and cream. Plant sources of saturated fats include palm oil, palm kernel oil, and coconut oil.
• Avoid foods with partially hydrogenated oils in them. These contain trans fats. Examples are stick margarine, some tub margarines, cookies, crackers, and other baked goods.
• Avoid fried foods.
General information
• Eat more home-cooked food and less restaurant, buffet, and fast food.
• Limit or avoid alcohol.
• Limit foods that are high in starch and sugar.
• Lose weight if you are overweight. Losing just 5–10% of your body weight can help your overall health and prevent diseases such as diabetes and heart disease.
• Monitor your salt (sodium) intake, especially if you have high blood pressure. Talk with your health care provider about your sodium intake.
• Try to incorporate more vegetarian meals weekly.
What foods can I eat?
Fruits
All fresh, canned (in natural juice), or frozen fruits.
Vegetables
Fresh or frozen vegetables (raw, steamed, roasted, or grilled). Green salads.
Grains
Most grains. Choose whole wheat and whole grains most of the time. Rice and pasta, including brown rice and pastas made with whole wheat.
Meats and other proteins
Lean, well-trimmed beef, veal, pork, and lamb. Chicken and turkey without skin. All fish and shellfish. Wild duck, rabbit, pheasant, and venison. Egg whites or low-cholesterol egg substitutes. Dried beans, peas, lentils, and tofu. Seeds and most nuts.
Dairy
Low-fat or nonfat cheeses, including ricotta and mozzarella. Skim or 1% milk (liquid, powdered, or evaporated). Buttermilk made with low-fat milk. Nonfat or low-fat yogurt.
Fats and oils
Non-hydrogenated (trans-free) margarines. Vegetable oils, including soybean, sesame, sunflower, olive, peanut, safflower, corn, canola, and cottonseed. Salad dressings or mayonnaise made with a vegetable oil.
Beverages
Water (mineral or sparkling). Coffee and tea. Diet carbonated beverages.
Sweets and desserts
Sherbet, gelatin, and fruit ice. Small amounts of dark chocolate.
Limit all sweets and desserts.
Seasonings and condiments
All seasonings and condiments.
The items listed above may not be a complete list of foods and beverages you can eat. Contact a dietitian for more options.
What foods are not recommended?
Fruits
Canned fruit in heavy syrup. Fruit in cream or butter sauce. Fried fruit. Limit coconut.
Vegetables
Vegetables cooked in cheese, cream, or butter sauce. Fried vegetables.
Grains
Breads made with saturated or trans fats, oils, or whole milk. Croissants. Sweet rolls. Donuts. High-fat crackers, such as cheese crackers.
Meats and other proteins
Fatty meats, such as hot dogs, ribs, sausage, bacon, rib-eye roast or steak. High-fat deli meats, such as salami and bologna. Caviar. Domestic duck and goose. Organ meats, such as liver.
Dairy
Cream, sour cream, cream cheese, and creamed cottage cheese. Whole milk cheeses. Whole or 2% milk (liquid, evaporated, or condensed). Whole buttermilk. Cream sauce or high-fat cheese sauce. Whole-milk yogurt.
Fats and oils
Meat fat, or shortening. Cocoa butter, hydrogenated oils, palm oil, coconut oil, palm kernel oil. Solid fats and shortenings, including bacon fat, salt pork, lard, and butter. Nondairy cream substitutes. Salad dressings with cheese or sour cream.
Beverages
Regular sodas and any drinks with added sugar.
Sweets and desserts
Frosting. Pudding. Cookies. Cakes. Pies. Milk chocolate or white chocolate. Buttered syrups. Full-fat ice cream or ice cream drinks.
The items listed above may not be a complete list of foods and beverages to avoid. Contact a dietitian for more information.
Summary
• Heart-healthy meal planning includes limiting unhealthy fats, increasing healthy fats, and making other diet and lifestyle changes.
• Lose weight if you are overweight. Losing just 5–10% of your body weight can help your overall health and prevent diseases such as diabetes and heart disease.
• Focus on eating a balance of foods, including fruits and vegetables, low-fat or nonfat dairy, lean protein, nuts and legumes, whole grains, and heart-healthy oils and fats.
This information is not intended to replace advice given to you by your health care provider. Make sure you discuss any questions you have with your health care provider.

Ventricular Assist Device Home Guide
It is important to follow instructions from your health care provider about caring for your ventricular assist device (VAD) at home. You will continue to work with a health care provider who specializes in VADs (VAD coordinator) and a heart specialist (cardiologist).
How to care for the VAD
Check the area around your VAD tube for signs of infection. Do this every day, or as often as told by your health care provider. Check for:
• Redness.
• Swelling.
• Blood or fluid coming from the opening.
• Warmth.
• A bad smell.
Check the following numbers every day. Write them down.
• Your temperature.
• Your blood pressure.
• Your weight.
• The VAD speed (rpm).
• The VAD pulsatility index (PI).
• The VAD power.
• The VAD flow (L/min).
How to change the bandage around the VAD
You will have a bandage (dressing) around the area where the VAD tube exits your abdomen. The dressing consists of a drain sponge, gauze, and adhesive tape. Your VAD coordinator may help you order the supplies that you need to change your dressing.
To remove your VAD dressing and put on a new dressing, do the following steps:
1. Put on a mask.
2. Wash your hands with soap and water.
3. Put on sterile gloves.
4. Remove the dressing and throw it away. Do not touch the VAD tubing or the skin near it after you remove the dressing.
5. Remove your gloves and put on a new pair of sterile gloves.
6. Clean the area around the VAD tube. Use a sterile cleaning solution as told by your health care provider.
7. Gently dry your skin with sterile gauze.
8. Apply the drain sponge to the VAD tubing site. Cover the drain sponge with a gauze pad.
9. Secure the dressing with adhesive tape.
Change your dressing as often as told by your health care provider.
Traveling with a VAD
• Get permission from your health care provider before you travel. You will need a letter from your health care provider that explains your medical condition and VAD equipment.
• Make sure that your VAD coordinator can reach you when you travel.
• Find VAD centers and health care facilities close to your travel destinations.
• Do not pass through metal detectors or radiation detectors. Security may need to inspect your external VAD equipment.
• Always keep the following items with you:
◦ Extra equipment for your VAD (power pack and charged batteries).
◦ Phone numbers for your emergency contacts.
Follow these instructions at home:
Medicines
• Take over-the-counter and prescription medicines only as told by your health care provider.
• If you were prescribed an antibiotic or blood-thinning medicine, take it as told by your health care provider. Do not stop taking the antibiotic even if you start to feel better.
Activity
• Return to your normal activities as told by your health care provider. Ask your health care provider what activities are safe for you.
• Avoid physical activity in very hot or very cold weather.
• Do not vacuum.
• Do not play contact sports or do intense physical activities.
• Do not drive or use heavy machinery.
Lifestyle
• Do not use any products that contain nicotine or tobacco, such as cigarettes, e-cigarettes, and chewing tobacco. If you need help quitting, ask your health care provider.
• Avoid places where you may be exposed to secondhand smoke.
• Do not sleep on your abdomen.
• If you drink alcohol:
◦ Limit how much you use to:
▪ 0–1 drink a day for women.
▪ 0–2 drinks a day for men.
◦ Be aware of how much alcohol is in your drink. In the U.S., one drink equals one 12 oz bottle of beer (355 mL), one 5 oz glass of wine (148 mL), or one 1½ oz glass of hard liquor (44 mL).
Bathing
• Do not expose the VAD to water. This can cause VAD pump failure.
• Cover your VAD equipment when you shower. Your health care provider will show you how to do this.
• Do not take baths, swim, or use a hot tub until your health care provider approves. Ask your health care provider if you may take showers. You may only be allowed to take sponge baths.
General instructions
• Make sure you understand:
◦ The parts of your VAD and how they work.
◦ The VAD alarm functions.
◦ How to change your VAD dressing.
◦ What to do in case of an emergency.
• When leaving home, take a spare Swanson controller and extra VAD batteries with you.
• Keep all follow-up visits as told by your health care provider. This is important. You will need to have blood tests frequently.
Contact a health provider if you:
• Have swelling in your feet, ankles, or legs.
• Gain more than 3 lb (1.36 kg) in 1 day.
• Have signs of infection (fever, redness, pain, swelling, warmth, or a bad smell) in the area where your VAD tube exits your abdomen.
• Feel nauseous, vomit, or have pain in your abdomen.
• Have a lot of bruises.
• Have blood or fluid coming from the opening.
See your VAD coordinator if you:
• Have questions or concerns about your VAD.
• Need to order supplies for your VAD.
• Notice a VAD flow rate, PI, or power level that is abnormal.
Get help right away if:
• You have:
◦ Difficulty breathing.
◦ Chest pain.
◦ Pain that spreads to your arm, neck, jaw, back, or abdomen.
◦ Blood in your vomit or your stool.
• You cough up blood.
• Your VAD stops working or loses power.
• Your VAD becomes damaged.
• A VAD alarm goes off.
• You have any symptoms of a stroke. "BE FAST" is an easy way to remember the main warning signs of a stroke:
◦ B - Balance. Signs are dizziness, sudden trouble walking, or loss of balance.
◦ E - Eyes. Signs are trouble seeing or a sudden change in vision.
◦ F - Face. Signs are sudden weakness or numbness of the face, or the face or eyelid drooping on one side.
◦ A - Arms. Signs are weakness or numbness in an arm. This happens suddenly and usually on one side of the body.
◦ S - Speech. Signs are sudden trouble speaking, slurred speech, or trouble understanding what people say.
◦ T - Time. Time to call emergency services. Write down what time symptoms started.
• You have other signs of a stroke, such as:
◦ A sudden, severe headache with no known cause.
◦ Nausea or vomiting.
◦ Seizure.
These symptoms may represent a serious problem that is an emergency. Do not wait to see if the symptoms will go away. Get medical help right away. Call your local emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Do not drive yourself to the hospital.
Summary
• Check the area around your VAD tube for signs of infection. Do this every day, or as often as told by your health care provider.
• When leaving home, take a spare Swanson controller and extra VAD batteries with you.
• Return to your normal activities as told by your health care provider. Ask your health care provider what activities are safe for you.
• Make sure you know when you need to contact your VAD coordinator.
This information is not intended to replace advice given to you by your health care provider. Make sure you discuss any questions you have with your health care provider.
